# Controlled test fixtures

All Windows fixtures use generated, owned locations under `.artifacts/` in this repository. The full-disk fixture additionally uses an ephemeral UUID-named WSL2 `tmpfs` mount under `/mnt`, never a user volume.
Never pass a user document to fault injection, deletion, replacement, or corruption tests.

- Rust integration tests create a unique UUID directory per case under `.artifacts/T003/`. `authorized` and sibling `outside` are both test-owned; a real Windows junction intentionally points between them to prove grant rejection.
- No recursive cleanup is performed by these tests. Any future cleanup must resolve and validate the absolute test root before deleting, and must not traverse a junction target.
- Web tests explicitly identify their mock bridge. Plain browser mode produces a visible IPC error; it never synthesizes successful native file operations.
- Web E2E now builds the frontend and serves it with local Vite preview, matching the frontend embedded in Tauri. Dev-server module/HTML transformation waits previously exhausted per-test navigation timeouts; both failed traces are retained under T102. The 30-second test limit, retries and worker configuration remain unchanged. Build-preview tests still use explicit mock IPC and do not establish native IO, development hot reload or Release startup performance.
- Desktop tests spawn a real compiled Tauri binary and attach to its real WebView2 using CDP. Only this child gets a loopback debug port and an isolated E-drive WebView profile; no production test IPC is registered.
- The default desktop test creates Chinese/space/emoji-named files with random markers, multi-selects them through real native dialog controls, checks buffers/edit/undo/reopen, then CtrlS and exact UTF8/CRLF bytes. The second file remains unchanged until its explicit edit in the later save-all batch. An external change is preserved after a rejected save. A test-only wrapper in Tauri's existing debug callback table delays delivery of one real Ack: input stays dirty until the next save; no fake result/grant/disk IO or product delay command is used. This is response-latency injection, not a timing claim about naturally slow disk IO. The helper accepts only 1–8 controlled files and checks roots/hashes/executable/PID/parent worker; foreign workers are rejected. Current evidence is under `.artifacts/T102/`, historical T101/M0 remains T101/T002.
- The native save-all helper uses five controlled dirty documents: two actual writes, a real external-write conflict in the third, native chooser Cancel in the fourth, and an unprocessed fifth. It checks exact first/second bytes, preserves third external bytes and all three remaining buffers/dirty states. Web/TS tests separately cover clicking stop while awaiting an Ack; the separate full-disk scenario below covers native disk exhaustion.
- The desktop child receives `FEATHERPAD_USER_DATA_DIR` pointing inside its unique E-drive fixture profile. Product state-directory configuration changes only private local storage, never file grants. Tests do not write recovery/transaction state to the real user profile.
- `open-folder` accepts exactly one existing directory below the generated `webview2-*` root, rejects file/reparse/foreign paths, and verifies the spawned Tauri PID/executable hash/parent worker before driving the owned native folder dialog. The scenario creates Chinese/space/emoji names, a hidden file, read-only file, real junction, empty root, temporarily ACL-denied root and subdirectory, then restores ACLs and checks exact tree state. It also creates a 205-file real directory to prove the native UI's first 200-item page and one Load More action. Root replacement happens after a real dirty CodeMirror edit and checks that buffer/tab state survives.
- Rust `directories` integration tests use unique owned directories and real Windows filesystem attributes to cover one-level enumeration, natural/folder-first sorting, hidden filtering, cursor revision/filter binding, empty pages, invalid limits, file-vs-directory grants and relative/canonical escape rejection. Product enumeration holds no-delete parent/directory handles and verifies the opened directory's final path while listing. `directory_scale` creates 100,000 owned empty files only after explicit opt-in, uses a fixed 300ms Release budget, writes raw timing to `.artifacts/T104/directory-scale.json`, and removes only its generated UUID directory. JS restores ACLs, removes the junction itself, verifies each recursive-delete target below the per-test `webview2-*` fixture root, then removes only those generated paths.
- The same owned-process helper supports `action:save` for exactly one missing destination in the generated fixture directory and `action:cancel` with no files. Save-name Edit ID1001 under ComboBox differs from Open's 1148 container; both are matched by observed class/ID/ownership, with bounded initialization wait. Diagnostics contain owned test-dialog titles and control class/IDs, never document body. Native checks cover first-save cancel, exact UTF8/CRLF bytes, copy leaving source bytes/dirty unchanged, and a later ordinary save to the original destination.
- Existing destinations use `overwrite`, `confirm-system`, `inspect-overwrite`, `confirm-overwrite`, and `reject-overwrite`, with exactly one existing fixture and verified hash. Both native confirmation titles, destination text and unique enabled Yes/No controls must match. DirectUI text is read only from that owned dialog via existing UIAutomation system assemblies (maximum 100 Text elements), not the whole desktop. The actual button receives BM_CLICK; file-dialog submission is posted to avoid blocking on nested confirmation. Inspect sends no click and records `commandInvoked:false`. Tests prove overwrite cancellation, revision-captured external mutation refusal, successful same-ID binding, copy-over-source refusal, copy over another existing target without changing source bytes/dirty, and refusal to overwrite another open document.
- `inspect-hardlink`, `confirm-hardlink`, and `reject-hardlink` use the same controlled checks and a distinct exact native-dialog title. Node creates real Windows hardlinks in that child's fixture directory. CtrlS No retains both files and dirty text; Yes changes only the selected path and keeps its document ID; the old alias opens as a different document after replacement. External writes after native confirmation capture are rejected without overwriting either alias or buffer. While the dialog waits, real stat IPC succeeds and another request for the same document returns BUSY. These are real disk/IPC assertions.
- Rust `save_interruption` spawns its own integration-test executable, filtered to one test, with an owned UUID root and a private stdin barrier. Ready records bind nonce/PID/phase; parent checks liveness, then kills only that spawned process handle or releases a positive control. Real TemporaryReady and Committed states, original/body/temporary bytes, hashes, markers and a fresh service reopen are checked. No ignored tests or production hooks are used. Results stay under `.artifacts/T102/interruptions/`; these are native core termination tests, not Tauri session recovery or power-loss tests.
- The desktop test ends by holding one real native SaveAck in the existing framework debug callback table, after actual target/body/committed verification. It terminates only its own Tauri child and checks the files again. The native JSON records the receipt/hash and actual child exit result. This proves post-commit process termination, not automatic restart/session recovery.
- `tests/desktop/disk-full.ts` mounts a unique 16 MiB WSL2 `tmpfs`, opens a tiny hash-checked source through the real OS chooser, fills the backing filesystem to `ENOSPC`, and saves through the real Tauri Release. The helper accepts `open-fault` only for the manifest-bound UUID mount and ownership token. Tests assert source bytes/hash unchanged, dirty editor retained, `write-temporary` failure visible, and recovery manifest/body/original consistency; cleanup lazy-detaches and removes the mount after the app exits.
- `open-degraded` allows exactly one owned, hash-matched file of 2097153 bytes; all other open/confirmation actions retain their prior small-fixture limits. The native test builds complete LF text with a final sentinel, opens through the OS chooser, inserts Chinese/emoji in real CodeMirror and verifies the entire saved byte sequence. Rust separately checks 2 MiB ±1, 20 MiB −1 and Unicode long-line thresholds. Chunked/head-preview and performance observations use the separate fixtures and evidence below.
- `open-large-chunk` accepts exactly one owned, hash-matched 20 MiB text file; `open-head-preview` accepts exactly one owned, hash-matched 100 MiB + 1 byte text file. The native test uses the real chooser/IPC path, pages backward and forward through 64 KiB readonly chunks with a single-page DOM limit, verifies the source hash, requires an explicit preview action for the larger file, and checks readonly save controls. Rust separately covers all 2/20/100 MiB boundaries, revision/handle failures, UTF-8/UTF-16 windows, and real disk growth across the 20/100 MiB limits during a read. These tests use actual files; no grant or IO result is mocked.
- `Measure-ProcessTree.ps1` samples only the spawned Tauri child and descendants by PID and records private and working-set bytes. T103 captured one Win11 development observation after a long mixed-scenario run; it is not a clean performance run or a 10-sample p95.
- `FEATHERPAD_CHOOSER_AUTOMATION=manual` waits for a person to select the generated file recorded in `.artifacts/T002/chooser-fixture.json`. `FEATHERPAD_VERIFY_CHOOSER=0` explicitly limits a run to shell/IPC checks and records `nativeChooserVerified:false`; such a run cannot satisfy the G0 picker acceptance. A timeout is a failure, never a skip or pass.
- Default `pnpm test:desktop` targets the Release binary; `FEATHERPAD_DESKTOP_PROFILE=debug` explicitly selects a dev build (requires the local dev server). The result JSON states which profile and executable hash was tested.
